name: template_descent_block_resynthesis
precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz and two_qubit; min_qubits 2, max_qubits 20; applies to any Clifford+Rz op list that partitions into width<=4 blocks containing at least 2 cx and at least 3 rotations. Circuits without multi-qubit blocks (pure 1-qubit chains) are excluded and cost nothing.
identity: Skeleton-shrinking block resynthesis (template descent + instantiation), as opposed to angle fixing on a fixed skeleton. For each block B from blocks.partition(circuit, width<=4, max_gates=40): (1) form the exact local unitary U = sim.unitary(B.local_ops, B.k) (k<=4, so at most 16x16); (2) take B's own Clifford skeleton as template T0 and enumerate reduced templates T1, T2, ... by deleting ONE two-qubit gate at a time (and the rotation slots that become adjacent-mergeable), ordered by the deleted cx's contribution to the block's entangling power (smallest first), each reduced template re-expressed by refit.euler_template with one rz slot per surviving single-qubit position; (3) for each candidate template, fit its angle vector by refit.least_squares against U from several deterministic restarts (the previous template's fitted angles with the deleted slot's angle set to 0, plus a fixed pseudo-random restart set), giving Fit(angles, distance); (4) accept the SMALLEST template whose fitted phase-aligned operator distance is <= the block's share d_B of the drawn budget and whose priced cost (T-count under eps_rz = eps_synth/N_Rz, then qubits, then CNOT) is strictly lower than the block's current cost; recurse (try to delete one more two-qubit gate from the accepted template) until no candidate fits; (5) on the survivor only, spend the block's unspent remainder with refit.pin_to_grid to push any further angles onto the pi/4 grid. Splice back with blocks.splice. The distinguishing step is (2)+(3): DPF keeps the skeleton fixed and only moves angles; this REPLACES the skeleton with a strictly shorter one whenever the block's true reachable-manifold dimension is below the parameter count TKET's peephole output happens to carry, and refits ALL angles, not just the unpinned ones.
correctness: Each partition block is dependency-contiguous, so substituting its local op list by any V is a valid rewrite of the whole circuit: the global unitary changes from ... U ... to ... V ..., and by unitary invariance and subadditivity of the operator norm the end-to-end phase-aligned distance is bounded by the sum of the per-block distances ||V_B - U_B||_op (phase-aligned, since global phase is unobservable). Each accepted block therefore charges exactly its measured distance d_B to the shared ledger, and sum_B d_B <= the amount drawn. The fits themselves are not trusted: sim.hs_distance on the exact 2^k x 2^k matrices gives the number the frozen judge will charge, and the judge re-verifies every application (phase-aligned operator distance on the changed window, plus the one whole-circuit check per pass against the ORIGINAL circuit), so a template whose least-squares fit is a local minimum that does not reach U is simply rejected, never accepted on the optimizer's word. Soundness of the descent order does not matter for correctness, only for how much it finds: deleting a cx can only shrink the reachable set, so a fit that succeeds certifies that U lies on the smaller template's manifold to within d_B.
trigger: Run over blocks.blocks_with_rotations(circuit, minimum=3) restricted to blocks with k >= 2 and at least 2 two-qubit gates. A block is a match iff at least one reduced template reaches fitted distance <= its share AND the priced cost strictly falls; the number of off-grid rotations in the replacement must be strictly smaller than in the block (pure cx reductions at equal rotation count are also kept, since cost order breaks ties on CNOT). Blocks with 0 or 1 two-qubit gates, or whose best reduced fit stalls above its share, are skipped with no edit and no spend (budget.trial / refund around every attempt).
expected_effect: hhl_8 after the book has 439 off-grid rotations at eps_rz = 2.28e-6, i.e. ~57 T each, which is essentially all of the 26137. The circuit is TKET-FullPeepholeOptimise'd output of unitary-synthesised HHL blocks (693 h, 547 cx, 419 distinct generic angles, trigrams 'h rz h' and 'h s cx'): TKET squashes single-qubit chains and does 2-qubit KAK, but never resynthesises width-3/4 blocks, so structured HHL blocks (controlled eigenvalue-inversion rotations, QFT phase ladders) are carried in skeletons with more cx and more rotation slots than their true manifold needs. Each deleted cx typically removes 1-3 rotation slots. Expect ~80 off-grid rotations removed (439 -> ~360), which also lowers eps_rz' = 5e-4/360 and so the per-rotation gridsynth cost, landing near 21-22k T; the cx count falls too (secondary cost key). Nearly all of the drawn error is insurance: on blocks that really are over-parameterised the fit reaches ~1e-12, so the realised spend should be far below 2.5e-4, leaving the rest of the pool for other rules.
source: Younis, Sen, Yelick, Iancu, 'QFAST / QSearch: Quantum circuit synthesis by topology-aware template descent' (2020-2021) and Davis et al., 'Towards optimal topology-aware quantum circuit synthesis' (QSearch/LEAP, BQSKit) - template enumeration plus numerical instantiation (QFactor) of a fixed skeleton; the Cartan/KAK parameter-count bound (Vidal-Dawson, Shende-Bullock-Markov) is what makes a deleted cx a real dimension drop.
